records.description: Gandhi's own political writings and campaigns are a central source for this tradition; internal tensions and changes over time remain important.
Ambedkar's writings are foundational sources; later Ambedkarite movements are not identical to his complete body of thought.
The tradition is named for and draws heavily on Nehru's writings and political practice.
Roy participated in communist politics before developing Radical Humanism; this relationship is period-specific, not a lifelong label.
Locke is a major early modern source for rights, consent and political authority debates.
Rawls is a major source for contemporary liberal egalitarian political philosophy.
Mao's writings and revolutionary practice are associated with this tradition; doctrine and state outcomes must be separately assessed.
Bhagat Singh participated in revolutionary anti-colonial politics; his own writings should guide interpretation.
Bose was a major anti-colonial leader whose alliances and political proposals require historical contextualisation.
Tagore engaged with nationalism critically; this is a relationship of debate, not simple ideological membership.
No direct membership is asserted; classical statecraft is included as comparative context only.
